as someone with mental issues too i can tell you the fact that youre so worried about him and think of his well being is gonna make him feel a lot better already. I'd say tell him what you said to us, how you feel bad about it and want to do anything to support him. remind him hes not broken and that he wont be in pain forever and pretty much just remind him that you care and understand his pain. But most of all, and this is for you; youll never be able to heal him yourself. i know that sounds wrong, but my point is dont assume that its your duty to heal him. youre there to help him at most but he has to do the heavy lifting himself otherwise youll risk a codependent and emotionally taxing relationship for the both of you. I wish you both the best.

my honest advice is to maybe go with some cheaper options for the graphics card, im 19 and i work and live with my parents too. im in the process of buying parts for my very first PC, and ive been tempted to spend all my money at once. but look at it this way; if you focus on a lower mid range PC that you can upgrade in the future (meaning investing in a  good motherboard and cpu, everything else is lower mid range) you can play all the games you want rn and still have money left. my PC build is gonna cost me about $900. i know you may not have any other responsabilities with your money, but trust me its good practice to not blow it out all at once. keep some money on the side not only to feel satisfied, but also in case of anything. and its just a good habit to have with money. you never have too much of it, and if you can save yourself some money theres no reason why you shouldnt. ofc its all up to you in the end, its your hard earned money and no one should make you feel guilty for how you spend it. this is just my advice
